verdict_text: NO. The `save_sharded_safetensors` function only starts a new shard when the *cumulative* running total would exceed the cap (`if cur and cur_size + size > max_bytes`); it never isolates a specific tensor once it fits within the remaining budget. Since `model.embed_tokens.weight`/`lm_head.weight` (~412 MB each) are individually well under the 536,870,912-byte cap, the greedy loop will pack several subsequent small layer tensors alongside them until the cumulative total exceeds the cap, rather than placing them alone. This violates the explicit Output requirement in Required result §4: "A single tensor larger than that (here `model.embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight`... ) is stored alone in its own shard." Since Grading explicitly checks "sharding rules" and "exact key set" against the hidden reference, this shard-layout mismatch would fail grading even though the merge math itself (scale, `B @ A`, no transpose, dtype, required checks) is correct.
